Print a unit alone

Source: R/unit-names.R
fmt_unit.Rd

fmt_unit() prints the unit of a quantity, or of a string read as u() reads a unit, with no number: for a heading or a table column. It is a weft_text of length one with no printed record and no unit attributes, so fmt_cap() works on it.

Usage

fmt_unit(x, unit_form = NULL, unit = NULL)

Arguments

x

A quantity of any length (a missing value is allowed: no number prints), or one string naming a unit.

unit_form

NULL (the setting unit_form, else "auto"), "auto", "symbol" or "name". "none" is a weft_construct_error.

unit

A unit to convert x to first, as a string, or a ladder of units (one string with | between the units, or a character vector; see fmt_num()).

Value

A weft_text of length one.

Details

"auto" and "symbol" print the symbol text ("mg/L"; a unit with no symbol prints its name); "name" prints the name ("milligrams per litre"). The name is plural unless x has length one and its number prints "1" (a string takes the plural). A unit with no name is a weft_value_error; add one under units: in _weft.yml. A name there that is written with markdown needs its own plural:, as the English plural is added to the end of the markup (*site* would print *site*s). .cap leaves a symbol as it is, since its case is its meaning, and capitalises a name. unit converts x first, a string as well as a quantity; the unit of a formatter's text is not read, so pass the quantity. With a ladder of units (unit = "mm|m|km", rule 4.4.23) and a quantity, the unit is picked as fmt_num() picks it for x (one number, or the vector rule), and printed plural unless x has length one and prints "1"; a ladder of more than one unit with a string is a weft_value_error.

Examples

fmt_unit(u(5, mg/L))
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "mg/L"
fmt_unit(u(5, mg/L), unit_form = "name")
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "milligrams per litre"
